project.name: modernize-pro-data
project.description: Data migration tool for the Japanese financial sector targeting fully air-gapped customer sites. Coordinator (HQ) / Worker (field) split over REST+WebSocket; Spring Boot backend with an embedded DuckDB rule engine and a React operator frontend; shipped as a jpackage/MSI desktop bundle.

tour.title: Project Overview & Onboarding
tour.description: Start here. CLAUDE.md is the authoritative one-page brief: a data-migration tool for Japan's air-gapped financial sites, split into a Coordinator (HQ, owns the meta DB) and field Workers that talk back only over REST + WebSocket. ONBOARDING.md then expands every subsystem in depth -- the 9-phase project model, the four-stage pipeline, the rule engine, and the snapshot model -- and is the document the rest of this tour walks through in code form.

tour.title: Architectural Map
tour.description: Before reading code, get the lay of the land. The codebase splits into eight layers: a React frontend (presentation + state/API client), three backend layers (API & coordination, the migration engine, and a shared kernel), plus the CLI, the desktop installer/launcher, and project config. Foundational layers (shared kernel, migration engine) are depended upon by the API and frontend layers, so the tour explains them roughly bottom-up after the entry points.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & App Shell
tour.description: main.tsx mounts the root and renders a fallback error screen on failure; App.tsx wires the router, an ErrorBoundary, and the license/language bootstrap, mounting every page behind ProtectedRoute. AppShell.tsx is the operator UI's chrome -- sidebar, top bar, tab bar, notifications, and all global modals -- and has the highest fan-out on the frontend, making it the natural hub to read first.
tour.languageLesson: React apps bootstrap by calling createRoot().render() in the entry module (main.tsx). The router and an ErrorBoundary are mounted once at the App root so all pages inherit routing and crash isolation.

tour.title: Frontend State & API Client
tour.description: Building on the shell, this is how the UI holds data and talks to the backend. client.ts is the fetch wrapper used by nearly every page (fan-in 32): it attaches the auth token, unwraps the standard response envelope, raises ApiError, and logs out on a missing license. The zustand workspace store holds sites/projects/environments and the active selection, while the auth store holds the current session -- both among the most depended-upon modules in the frontend.
tour.languageLesson: zustand stores are plain hooks created with create(); the persist middleware mirrors selected slices to localStorage. Cross-user state (audit, notifications) is deliberately NOT persisted -- the backend audit_log is the single source of truth.

tour.title: Operator Workflow Pages
tour.description: These pages embody the day-to-day operator flow. MappingPage is the core workspace: AS-IS/TO-BE inventory, binding editors, and rule authoring with SQL/Java highlighting. ExecutionPage drives a run with preflight gating, table selection, live pipeline-stage progress, and start/stop/retry. VersionsPage exposes the snapshot diff view and the Request Review gate. ws.ts feeds them live run updates over STOMP WebSocket -- the field-to-HQ telemetry channel.

tour.title: Backend Entry & Security
tour.description: Crossing to the backend: ModernizeProDataApplication.java bootstraps the Spring Boot Coordinator/Worker process. SecurityConfig enforces stateless sessions, disables CSRF, and whitelists only anonymous endpoints (auth, health, license setup, worker enrollment). JwtAuthFilter validates bearer tokens and re-checks the session against the user record on every request -- the gate every API call from Step 4's client.ts passes through.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Boot uses @SpringBootApplication to enable component scanning and auto-configuration. Security filters extend OncePerRequestFilter so token validation runs exactly once per request before controllers see it.

tour.title: Shared Kernel: Response Envelope
tour.description: Two of the highest fan-in classes in the whole backend live here. ApiResponse is the standard success envelope and ApiException the standard error -- the GlobalExceptionHandler turns thrown ApiExceptions into the ErrorResponse shape that Step 4's client.ts unwraps. Understanding this contract makes every controller in the next steps readable at a glance.

tour.title: Run Orchestration & Phase Model
tour.description: This is the heart of the migration engine. RunController starts single and bulk runs, gating each by phase and run-type, aborts runs, and serves run history. RunService is the lifecycle brain: it resolves phase/runType, enforces the gating rules from Step 1's phase model, and completes/fails/aborts/times-out runs while advancing phases. StageInstance (fan-in 23) is the JPA entity for one stage execution within a run -- the unit every pipeline stage operates on.

tour.title: The Migration Pipeline Stages
tour.description: A run executes an ordered sequence of StageRunner stages -- the README's Extract -> Transform -> Load -> Verify -> Audit pipeline. CheckStage runs preflight validation; ExtractStage loads source CSV into DuckDB with correct encoding; TransformStage compiles mapping rules into DuckDB SQL and materializes the TO-BE shape (routing failures to quarantine); LoadStage COPYs into PostgreSQL; VerifyStage compares per-PK values for load fidelity; AuditStage runs data-quality checks. LocalWorkerExecutor drives this sequence in-process honoring cancellation.

tour.title: DuckDB Rule Engine & UDFs
tour.description: The Transform stage's power comes from an embedded DuckDB engine plus Java UDFs. DuckDbService manages the singleton DuckDB connection, spill config, bundled encodings/ICU extensions, and UDF registration. UdfRegistry wires in every custom function. The UDFs are domain-specific to Japanese mainframe data: UnpackCompUdf decodes COMP-3 packed-decimal from EBCDIC sources, ConvertEraUdf turns Japanese era dates into ISO dates. SqlComposer builds the FROM/JOIN and column aliases for the transform query from a binding's rules.

tour.title: Loading Into PostgreSQL
tour.description: After transformation, data lands in the TO-BE database via PgCopyManager, which wraps PostgreSQL's COPY protocol: it opens connections, truncates targets, toggles constraints for speed, and bulk-copies from CSV or a JDBC ResultSet. This is the workhorse behind Step 9's LoadStage and the reason the tool can move large mainframe extracts efficiently inside a closed network.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL COPY is far faster than row-by-row INSERT for bulk loads. Disabling constraints/indexes during the copy and re-enabling them afterward avoids per-row validation overhead.

tour.title: Mapping & DDL Import
tour.description: The pipeline needs definitions to execute. MappingTableBinding (fan-in 20) binds an AS-IS source set to a TO-BE target table. MappingImportService parses mapping/code CSVs, derives transform rules and bindings, and builds the DuckDB transform SQL that Step 10 runs. DdlImportService parses imported Oracle DDL into table/column metadata and advances or demotes the project phase based on AS-IS/TO-BE completeness -- linking schema import directly to the phase model from Step 1.

tour.title: Snapshot & Approval Subsystem
tour.description: Mappings are versioned and approved through snapshots. The Snapshot entity freezes mapping data, a change summary, and the execution context with version generation. SnapshotController exposes create / request-review / approve / reject / set-baseline / restore -- the gate behind Step 5's VersionsPage. SnapshotMappingRestoreService re-inserts rules, code maps, and bindings to roll a project back to any snapshot. This is how the air-gapped workflow guarantees only reviewed mappings ever run a cutover.

tour.title: Coordinator-Worker Distribution
tour.description: Recall the HQ/field split from Step 1. WorkerNodeService handles Worker self-registration (URL + token), heartbeat updates, revocation with session invalidation, and online-status resolution. WorkerDispatcher sends run lifecycle commands (start, cancel, ping) to remote Workers over WebSocket -- the same channel Step 5's ws.ts subscribes to. Together they let an isolated field Worker execute Step 9's pipeline while the Coordinator retains all authority and the meta DB.

tour.title: Packaging, PostgreSQL & Deployment
tour.description: Finally, how it all ships to a closed site. Launcher.java is the JavaFX desktop launcher that reads installer registry choices and routes to Worker vs Coordinator mode, driving Worker enrollment. PgManagedLifecycle unzips the bundled PostgreSQL, runs initdb, and manages start/stop via pg_ctl. main.wxs is the WiX/MSI package definition. compose.yaml stands up the meta DB and TO-BE PostgreSQL for local development. application.yml ties datasource, HikariCP, and Flyway-managed schema together.
tour.languageLesson: jpackage bundles a Java app with its own JRE into a native installer, so the closed site needs no pre-installed Java. WiX (.wxs) declaratively describes the MSI: features, components, and install directories compiled into the final package.
